title: Nvidia Stock News (Oct 14, 2026): NVDA Rises 1.0% to $228.52
summary: Nvidia closed at $228.52 on Oct 13, up 0.97% as the Nasdaq slipped 0.15%. What moved NVDA, how chip peers traded and the key risks.
body_markdown:
Chip stocks split.[AMD (AMD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amd/) rose 1.90%, Intel gained 1.44% and[TSMC (TSM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/tsm/) added 0.17%, while[Micron (MU)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mu/) dropped 3.62% and ASML lost 1.86%. Nvidia now sits 6.10% below its 52-week high of $243.37 and 39.11% above its 52-week low of $164.27.


## Why Nvidia Stock Rose


No fetched source names a company-specific reason for Tuesday's gain, so the move is best read against the indices and a mixed chip group. The most notable company headline of the day was about Nvidia's investments in Europe.


According to[GuruFocus](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-using-cash-build-next-212648081.html) , Nvidia agreed to buy a minority stake in Doctolib, citing a Reuters report dated October 13. Doctolib said it is "working with Nvidia to build new AI solutions." The size of the deal was not disclosed. GuruFocus also reported that Genesis AI named Nvidia a strategic investor and described the deals as small next to Nvidia's chip business, aimed at early positions in sectors that may later need more computing power.


Separately, as reported by[24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bought-semiconductor-fund-500-000-210309579.html) , Nvidia made up 17.55% of the VanEck Semiconductor ETF as of its June 30, 2026 filing, roughly double the next-largest holding, TSMC, at 9.29%.


## NVDA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Per[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvidia-5-years-where-stock-222600294.html) , fiscal second-quarter revenue (quarter ended July 26) was $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, with net income up 126%.
- Motley Fool reports that Nvidia holds over 80% of the data center chip market, and that CFO Colette Kress estimated hyperscaler capital spending at "nearly $800 billion in 2026."
- GuruFocus says the European stakes extend Nvidia's ecosystem beyond data centers into potential future AI customers.


### Risks


- Motley Fool names the durability of AI demand as the main risk, noting that how long the AI boom lasts is unknown.
- Concentration cuts both ways: with Nvidia at 17.55% of the VanEck fund, 24/7 Wall St. notes that holders of that ETF carry heavy exposure to one company's results.
- Not every chip name rose: Micron's 3.62% drop shows the group did not move as one in this session.
